business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with elements of Islamic Sharia and ministerial administrative regulations
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United Kingdom Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1975)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing as amended by Law No. 8 of 2015 and Law No. 46 of 2018; Executive Regulations issued by the Central Bank of Egypt and the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA); Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; GAFI One-Stop-Shop implementing regulations; FRA UBO Register Rules pursuant to Cabinet Decree No. 1904 of 2018

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each individual UBO/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / competent passport authority of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Egypt is an Apostille Convention member since 14 December 2021)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder and its ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or appointed registrar in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization via the Egyptian Embassy where the issuer is from a non-Apostille state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation agent/attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the grantor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille followed by licensed Arabic translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / professional source-of-funds certificate for each UBO contributing capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution in the UBO's residential / corporate jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization upon express request of GAFI or the AML compliance officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, and signatories against the CBE/AML regulatory lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the FRA-issued locally designated persons and PEP database. Enhanced due diligence, written source-of-wealth explanations, and senior-management approval are required for any politically exposed person. Screening must be repeated upon any change of ownership, appointment of directors, or material capital modification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor One-Stop Shop Portal and the Egyptian Commercial Registry (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in Arabic. A Latin transliteration/English name may be registered as a secondary name. The name must conform to Law No. 159 of 1981 requirements, must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name, and must not violate public order, religious sanctity, or established trade name conventions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the incorporator may file a written administrative objection with the GAFI Name Committee within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a cover letter stating the basis of contestation, a copy of the rejected name clearance receipt, and any evidence of prior use or trademark registration. A decision is typically issued within 15 working days. Further recourse may be made to the Egyptian Administrative Court in accordance with the Council of State Law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not fully permissible for LLC incorporation. An actual physical registered address within Egypt is required for service of process and commercial registry jurisdiction. A serviced-office arrangement provided by a licensed business center is commonly accepted for low-risk internet retail operations, but the address must be active, monitored, and available for official correspondence and potential inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated 5% annual probability for a standard low-risk DTC internet retail entity. The likelihood may increase if the registered office is a shared serviced address or if changes to shareholding, capital, or UBO structure trigger verification visits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate law firm engaged by the client
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border LLC incorporation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018, Arts. 20, 26 and 42 (formation, management and representative authority of limited liability companies); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (GAFI one-stop-shop requirements)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registration Directorate; local Commercial Registration Office under the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Incorporation and Articles of Association (E'a'adat Al-Taasis) filed through the GAFI One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for Egyptian LLCs; however, the contributed capital must be fully paid before incorporation and covered by a bank certificate of deposit; no escrow account is mandated under the Companies Law for standard LLC formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each founder's subscription to the authorized share capital of the Company be and is hereby ratified, with quotas allotted in accordance with the Articles of Association; RESOLVED, that the temporary then permanent registered office within Egypt be adopted for the Company's statutory seat, and the office address be notified to GAFI and the Commercial Registry; RESOLVED, that [Full Name] be appointed General Manager and [Full Name] be appointed Company Secretary / Finance Officer, each with full authority to open bank accounts, complete taxes, and sign incorporation filings; RESOLVED, that the aforementioned officers be authorized to execute all documents, pay all fees, and take any required step to legally operationalize the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Online Portal / Commercial Registry Name Committee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit online name search and reservation application for the LLC name, together with three alternatives. Pay the reservation fee, receive the official name reservation certificate, and verify that the proposed name does not violate public order, existing trademarks, or prior registration.
required_dossiers: Copy of founders' national ID or passport
Power of attorney if filer is not a founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, resubmit with substitute names within 14 days; the rejection letter includes the exact legal basis and no re-filing fee is payable for the first substitution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office of the Egyptian Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the Notary Public with all founders or their legal representatives, verify national identity documents, confirm the Articles of Association conforms to mandatory legal clauses, and obtain the official notarized attestation of signatures and date.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association signed by all founders
Valid national ID or passport of each founder
Audited financial statements or certified corporate documents if a founder is a legal entity
Notarized power of attorney for any appointed representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary raises a correction, execute a supplemental correction deed via addendum signed before the same Notary Public and refile with the GAFI dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Share Capital Deposit Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles together with the name reservation certificate, bank capital deposit certificate, registered office lease evidence and incorporation declaration. Pay the GAFI statutory fees and receive the incorporation certificate issued in the Company name.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate evidencing fully paid share capital deposit
Registered office lease agreement or title deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query, address the deficiencies and resubmit amended pages within 15 calendar days; failure to cure leads to a fresh filing but prior fees are credited toward the new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry, Tax Card and Social Insurance Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Commercial Registration Office and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the GAFI incorporation certificate to the local Commercial Registry to obtain the commercial registry extract. Then register with ETA to obtain the operating tax card, and register the Company and its employees with the National Social Insurance Authority. This completes the legal operation of the entity.
required_dossiers: Founders' national IDs and corporate legal documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry refuses registration, request a written refusal, correct the contradictory documents, and apply for re-consideration through the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade within 20 days; any late registration fine may be waived if no intent is established.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment Gateway Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial banks subject to Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) directives and approved PSPs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporate bank account at a CBE-licensed bank using the incorporation certificate, tax card, board resolution and proof of address. Concurrently, begin onboarding to Shopify Payments / PayPal / Stripe through the Company's legal name and local bank account to enable payment acceptance in EGP and foreign currencies.
required_dossiers: Occupancy and utility bill for registered office
KYC forms and beneficial ownership declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first bank declines the account due to enhanced due diligence, request a reasoned non-acceptance letter and approach another licensed bank; CBE maintains a directory of basic corporate accounts that must be opened without excess documentation for non-complex LLCs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — no industrial manufacturing component; Industrial Development Authority (IDA) clearance is not required for DTC e-commerce under ISIC 4791.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Registry Certificate and Egyptian Tax Authority Tax Card (governing online retail operation); no separate industrial or physical manufacturing license is mandated.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable for non-industrial e-commerce; if later a fulfillment warehouse is added, the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) under Law No. 4 of 1994 would be the competent authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — online retail has no industrial EIA requirement; full EIA Report required only for industrial facilities or logistics centers exceeding prescribed storage limits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply in the default e-commerce configuration; any future warehouse shall comply with EEAA limits on municipal waste segregation, e-waste disposal and ambient noise.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not mandated for a pure office-only DTC brand; if a fulfillment or storage area is established, the Civil Defense Authority must audit fire exits, extinguishers, structural load capacity, electrical wiring and occupational safety signposts before occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Ministry of Finance; online services portal: eta.gov.eg; for customs: Egyptian Customs Authority (e-customs portal) shaheenalbetaa. The mandatory e-invoicing system is administered through ETA's integrated electronic invoice portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity without an Egyptian permanent establishment making taxable supplies in Egypt must register for VAT through the ETA online portal (or by postal filing) using: (1) copy of incorporation certificate from country of residence, (2) passport copies of directors and authorised signatories, (3) certified power of attorney appointing a local tax representative, and (4) evidence of the Egyptian business address or P.O. box. The ETA issues a unique Tax Identification Number (TIN) and a VAT Registration Certificate within up to 40 working days. Entities incorporated as an Egyptian LLC must obtain a tax card (بطاقة ضريبية) from the local tax office and register for income tax, VAT, payroll tax (if employees), and stamp duty subsequent to incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists; Egypt imposes entity-level corporate income tax on Egyptian LLCs regardless of foreign ownership. No pass-through or partnership-equivalent election is available for LLCs. Certain investment incentive elections under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (e.g., deduction of investment costs over staged periods, free-zone status election) may be available for qualifying projects. Egypt does not currently provide hybrid mismatch elections; OECD hybrid mismatch rules are not domestically enacted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover (Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by Law No. 8 of 2023 and Law No. 23 of 2024); foreign suppliers with economic activity in Egypt or making distance sales to Egyptian consumers above this threshold must register. Exports are subject to 0% VAT and do not trigger cancellation of registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory integrated e-invoicing and e-receipt system administered by ETA. Registered taxpayers must issue electronic XML invoices through approved systems using API integration (ETA's online clearance platform) in near-real time prior to delivery/acquisition. Invoices receive a Unique Invoice Identifier and QR code after fiscal clearance; failure to clear invoices triggers administrative penalties (EGP 20,000–100,000 per non-cleared invoice). B2C sales are covered by the e-receipt mandate for specific industries, including e-commerce and retail; will be extended nationwide. Taxpayers must use Treasury or ETA-approved electronic signature/certificates.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is allowed for (i) exported goods provided that the goods leave Egypt within a statutory timeframe and the exporter retains customs proof of export; (ii) services supplied to non-residents where the benefit of the service is effectively consumed abroad and the service qualifies as an exported service under the VAT Implementing Regulations; and (iii) supplies related to international transport (subject to bilateral exemptions). For DTC webstore exports, zero-rating is available if the seller holds valid supplier code, issues an export invoice, and receives payment from outside Egypt in freely convertible currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (single administrative document processed by Egyptian Customs Authority)
Bill of Lading (for sea freight) or Air Waybill (for air freight)
Commercial invoice showing 0% VAT and export destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing transfer of foreign currency from the foreign buyer/consumer into Egypt
Proof of foreign currency settlement to the Central Bank of Egypt (where applicable)
Contract or purchase order evidencing the export transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to heightened documentary review and ETA cross-matching with customs export records and CBE repatriation reports. A false or fraudulent zero-rating claim exposes the taxpayer to: reassessment at 14% VAT on the full export value; reversal of input VAT credits claimed on export-related purchases; pecuniary penalties up to twice the amount of tax evaded; criminal fines and imprisonment under VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 (Articles 46–55); and a 5% withholding tax certification penalty for incorrect invoices. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline renders the zero-rating claim void and the VAT output tax becomes due with late payment interest at 18% per annum.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Banking Supervision and Foreign Exchange Operations Sector
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified managed-float foreign-exchange regime following the March 2024 unification of the official and parallel exchange rates. The Egyptian Pound (EGP) is a convertible trade settlement currency but is not freely convertible outside the licensed banking system. Current-account transactions (DTC import/export of retail goods and cross-border digital services) are settled by CBE-licensed banks upon documentary verification; capital-account movements (share-subscription injections, dividend remittances, and liquidating distributions) are permitted but require bank-level registration, Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax clearance, and practical priority treatment within the bank's USD liquidity allocation. For an Egyptian LLC engaged in Shopify DTC retail, after-tax profit remittance is lawful and requires audited financial statements, a board dividend resolution, ETA confirmation of no outstanding tax arrears, and the CBE inward-investment registration; residual hurdles are operational timing delays during international reserve stress rather than statutory prohibition.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE rules, export proceeds must be fully repatriated into the Egyptian banking system within 120 days from the date of shipment (bill of lading date) or from the date of the customs declaration, with waiver extensions available for specified capital-goods transactions. Under the post-2024 unified-exchange-rate regime, the CBE does not publish a fixed statutory conversion percentage for surrendered proceeds; the absolute obligations are full repatriation through a CBE-licensed bank, retention in an Egyptian foreign-currency account, and priority offering of conversion to the relationship bank to fund essential-import demand. In practice, a Shopify DTC exporter may be requested by its bank to convert a portion of received USD (commonly 25-50% of net settlement) into EGP for local operating liquidity. All Shopify Payments, Stripe, and PayPal settlements must flow to the LLC's Egyptian bank account within the statutory window, and the PSP payout statements must be retained as the export-receipt evidence trail.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Dual-Currency Operational Account plus Export Proceeds Sub-account (EGP/USD)
Operational Settlement Account plus Capital Escrow Sub-account
Cross-Border Settlement Account with USD Nostro-Linked Routing
Specialized Export Receipts Account with CBE Reporting Integration

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: QNB Alahly Bank (Qatar National Bank Egypt)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for direct treasury settlement and Low for export-proceeds clearing. Offshore digital EMIs (Payoneer, Wise, Airwallex, Neat) are not licensed by the CBE as banks and cannot lawfully receive or settle Egyptian export proceeds in place of a CBE-licensed bank; routing export sales value through an unlicensed EMI exposes the LLC to AML review and breaches CBE repatriation requirements. Their permissible role is restricted to facilitating the collection of Shopify/PayPal/Stripe retail proceeds in USD and automatically sweeping funds to the LLC's Egyptian corporate account through the PSP's partner banking network. Licensed Egyptian fintechs and payment service providers (e.g., e-finance, Fawry, Valu) may be used for domestic EGP collection and acquiring services, but they do not provide FX conversion or cross-border treasury clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical onboarding is mandatory. CBE KYC regulations and bank-specific account-opening policies require at least one director, or a formally appointed authorized signatory under a notarized power of attorney, to attend an in-person interview at the Egyptian branch with an original passport or national ID, the LLC commercial-registry extract, the tax card, the board resolution appointing signatories, and proof of the registered office. Remote account opening for a newly formed Egyptian LLC is not available; foreign shareholders may authenticate corporate documents through Egyptian embassy legalization or apostille, but a local resident signatory with direct accountability must appear for the CBE interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or non-visible ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) situated in an offshore or low-substance jurisdiction, or a foreign holding company above the Egyptian LLC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificates of incorporation, register of beneficial owners, certified passports of ultimate individuals, GAFI acknowledgment of foreign shareholding, board resolutions, sworn source-of-funds declarations for the initial capital, and a written legal opinion from a licensed Egyptian attorney verifying the full ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented cross-border e-commerce receipt pattern using multiple PSP acquirers (Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe) with hundreds of low-value daily settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reconciliation pack comprising platform payout schedules, PSP monthly statements, order-level CSV exports, refund and chargeback reports, customer-invoice matching files, the registered domain/IP ownership certificate, trademark registration, the live Shopify storefront link, and a signed undertaking that no crypto-asset settlement is accepted and all disputed transactions are reversed through the PSP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared DTC retail business and sudden high-value FX conversion demands or bulk B2B-style account debits in the absence of visible operating history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A 12-month business plan with revenue forecasts, supplier purchase orders and contracts, courier and customs export documentation (airway bills, export declarations, e-commerce customs entries) linking the entity to physical goods flows, trade-channel agreements with carriers (DHL/FedEx/UPS), and a treasury KPI letter prepared by the bank's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or high-risk corridor exposure when customer geographies include GCC and MENA (Middle East and North Africa) card-acquiring regions or flagged jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer due diligence screening logs, privacy-compliant country-level sales analytics, contractual assurance that goods are low-risk physical consumer products free of dual-use or prohibited content, and an internal policy clause prohibiting sales to persons or territories subject to UN/EU/OFAC sanctions, supported by the LLC's published terms of sale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity injection must be remitted via SWIFT MT103/202 to the LLC's CBE-licensed Egyptian bank account, referencing the CBE Balance-of-Payments purpose code 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' and, where applicable, the GAFI investment certificate issued under Investment Law No. 72/2017. The receiving bank conducts AML verification, validates the share-subscription resolution and amended commercial-registry extract, issues the inward-remittance credit note, and updates the CBE foreign-investment register; funds are released to the EGP operational ledger after source-of-funds clearance. No mandatory lock-in applies to equity capital, but early dividend repatriation within a short ownership period attracts heightened ETA and banking scrutiny.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Overseas inventory purchases are settled through SWIFT MT103/203 (RMA-verified) for supplier invoices or through commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) issued by the Egyptian relationship bank and advised through a confirming bank for bulk shipments. Local EGP operating costs clear over the RTGS and Instant Payment Network (IPN) infrastructures. Every FX disbursement requires the CBE Form A import application, pro-forma invoice, underlying commercial contract, and shipping documents (bill of lading, airway bill, or courier waybill). Preferred rails for the Shopify DTC model are T/T advance or open-account settlement via MT103 and DP/DA documentary collections, with 60- to 120-day usance LCs reserved for larger inventory replenishment cycles.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery-based EGP/USD outright forward contracts matched to underlying export-receivable and import-payable trade exposures, executed only with CBE-licensed bank counterparties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in EGP/USD offered by CBE-regulated banks or their licensed offshore desks, documented against real trade flows and Board-approved risk policies
FX swaps combining an immediate EGP/USD spot transaction with an offsetting forward leg for intra-company liquidity management and funding rebalancing
Trade-linked structured deposits with embedded FX hedging components, permitted only where the risk is transparently disclosed and the bank confirms CBE regulatory parameters

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end; 30 April for a 31 December year-end LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine EGP 10,000–50,000; late-payment surcharge 2% per month; tax-card suspension and enforced collection by asset attachment; persistent default may trigger commercial strike-off via GAFI coordination.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (Partners' Adoption and GAFI Deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment (GAFI) / Central Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual partners' meeting within 3 months of fiscal year-end; audited statements deposited with GAFI immediately after adoption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unapproved statements bar lawful profit distribution; fines under Companies Law 72/2017; two consecutive years of non-filing trigger GAFI administrative strike-off and loss of investment incentives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days following the registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incremental daily fines for late renewal; suspension of registry extracts; continued non-renewal for one registration cycle triggers administrative strike-off and loss of limited liability standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually in conjunction with the Commercial Registry renewal; separately updated within 15 days of any shareholding transfer or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines and imprisonment under AML Law 80/2002 and Companies Law 72/2017; refusal of registry services; banking and payment-rail access restrictions for the Shopify DTC operation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Municipality Commercial License Office / GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal before 31 December of each operating calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative closure orders for unlicensed operation; fines up to EGP 20,000 per assessment; police/municipal seizure of e-commerce inventory in repeated default cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit under Companies Law 72/2017 where issued or paid-up capital equals or exceeds EGP 1,000,000, where the number of partners exceeds 10, or where GAFI/ETA mandates audited accounts due to regulated activity or investment incentives; all other LLCs must still attach reviewed financial statements to the CIT return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS, applicable to all corporate entities; full IFRS permitted for consolidated groups and entities listed on the Egyptian Exchange.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a statutory UBO register identifying each natural person holding, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of equity or voting rights or exercising ultimate control; any share transfer must be recorded in the partners' register and reported to GAFI within 15 days; the annual UBO confirmation is filed with the Commercial Registry renewal; nominee shareholding arrangements are prohibited under AML Law 80/2002, and concealment triggers fines and criminal sanctions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% of taxable net profit under the Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general reduced rate applies to an ordinary Egyptian LLC conducting internet retail. Tax holidays or investment incentives may apply only where the project satisfies the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, special economic-zone legislation, or other approved incentive regimes. Incentives are activity-, location-, approval-, and commencement-date dependent and must not be assumed for an ordinary Shopify DTC business. Deductible expenses must be directly related to business activity, properly documented, and not otherwise disallowed. Certain investment and development incentives may permit additional deductions or tax reductions under applicable legislation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate income tax return for legal persons, commonly filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority electronic tax return portal. The applicable electronic form designation and portal workflow should be confirmed against the current ETA release and the taxpayer's registration profile.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within four months following the end of the financial year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual deadline is 30 April of the following year. The return is due even where there is no taxable profit, subject to applicable exemption or deregistration rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ETA tax registration number, unified tax number, legal name, legal form, registered address, activity code, branch information, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An Egyptian LLC must use its Egyptian tax registration details. A non-resident owner or supplier is not substituted for the Egyptian legal entity as the corporate taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal-year start and end dates, accounting basis, and financial statement currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the period approved or legally applicable to the Egyptian LLC. Foreign parent reporting dates do not replace the Egyptian entity's local filing period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before Egyptian income tax, reconciled to the approved financial statements and accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the Egyptian LLC's accounts. Foreign group results, foreign branch income, and shareholder receipts must be separately analyzed and must not be merged without a legal basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income claimed to be exempt, excluded, treaty-relieved, or subject to a special regime, supported by the relevant legal provision and documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder's residence or treaty status does not exempt the Egyptian LLC's Egyptian-source operating profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs for expenses lacking business purpose, documentation, statutory deductibility, or arm's-length support; income tax itself is generally not deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related parties require contracts, invoices, proof of benefit, withholding-tax analysis, and transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting depreciation is reconciled to tax depreciation under applicable Egyptian rules, including treatment of equipment, software, leasehold improvements, and other capital assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-group depreciation schedules cannot be claimed unless they relate to assets owned or used by the Egyptian taxpayer and satisfy Egyptian documentation requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Inventory and cost of goods sold
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening inventory, purchases, import costs, customs, freight, landed cost, closing inventory, and write-downs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imported inventory must be supported by customs records, commercial invoices, shipping documents, foreign-exchange records, and related-party pricing evidence where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross DTC sales, refunds, discounts, chargebacks, shipping income, payment-processor settlements, and other operating revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Shopify, PayPal, Stripe, bank, and general-ledger data. Gross settlement amounts must be reconciled to fees, refunds, and customer receipts rather than reporting only net cash settlements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income and foreign tax credits claimed, subject to Egyptian credit limitations, documentary requirements, and applicable treaty provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are not automatic. Obtain foreign tax certificates, establish legal liability and payment, and apply the applicable Egyptian statutory and treaty limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases, sales, services, royalties, loans, guarantees, cost allocations, management charges, and other controlled transactions, with counterparty identity and values.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the foreign parent, affiliates, founders, directors, common-control entities, and beneficial owners. Use consistent amounts across the income tax return, withholding returns, financial statements, and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year taxable loss, carried-forward losses, utilization, and remaining balance, subject to the five-year limitation and applicable continuity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain year-by-year schedules. Accounting losses, foreign losses, and losses of another group company cannot automatically offset the Egyptian LLC's taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after statutory adjustments, applicable deductions, prior-year losses, credits, advance payments, and tax withheld at source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the final liability to advance payments, withholding certificates, and payments made through the ETA system. Do not offset foreign withholding against Egyptian corporate tax without legal support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic authentication, financial statements, auditor information where required, tax schedules, supporting reconciliations, and payment evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The authorized representative of the Egyptian LLC remains responsible for local filing. Group finance personnel may prepare data but should not replace the locally authorized signatory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incorrect filing may trigger statutory fines, tax assessment, examination, and additional tax for late payment. Egyptian tax law provides monetary penalties that may vary by violation and repetition; late-return penalties are commonly stated within statutory ranges that can reach EGP 5,000 to EGP 200,000, with higher ranges for repeated violations. Additional tax for delayed payment is generally calculated monthly under the applicable statutory rate, commonly 1.5% per month, subject to legislative changes. There is no general daily surcharge equivalent to a daily interest regime. Failure to file does not suspend the underlying tax liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian VAT return, generally filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority VAT/e-tax portal where the LLC is VAT-registered or required to register.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due by the end of the month following the relevant VAT period, subject to the taxpayer's registration category and current ETA instructions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable domestic supplies, applicable VAT rate, exempt supplies, zero-rated supplies, exports, and VAT collected.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign customer status does not automatically make a sale an export. Preserve evidence of place of supply, export clearance, delivery, and payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recoverable VAT on local purchases, imports, logistics, advertising, and operating costs, supported by valid tax invoices and customs documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign platform fees generally require separate reverse-charge, withholding, or imported-service analysis and are not treated as ordinary Egyptian input VAT without a valid basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Output VAT less allowable input VAT, prior credits, adjustments, and refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the return to sales platforms, payment processors, bank receipts, invoices, credit notes, and customs records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late VAT filing, underpayment, failure to issue compliant invoices, and unsupported input-VAT claims may result in statutory fines, denial of input credit, assessment of VAT, additional tax, and potential criminal exposure for deliberate evasion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Monthly withholding-tax declarations and payment records submitted through the Egyptian Tax Authority electronic tax system, where the LLC pays amounts subject to Egyptian withholding tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Withholding tax is generally remitted and reported within the statutory period following the month of payment or credit, subject to the applicable category and ETA procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax identification number, residence status, beneficial-owner information where relevant, and payment address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain a current foreign tax-residence certificate before applying treaty relief and retain evidence that the recipient is the beneficial owner where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, interest, royalties, technical or management services, commissions, rent, professional fees, or other payment classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify by legal substance and contract terms, not by the invoice label. Bundled software, advertising, platform, and service payments require separate analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross payment, domestic withholding rate, treaty rate if accepted, tax withheld, payment date, and remittance date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply a treaty rate solely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty country. Retain the treaty article, residence certificate, beneficial-ownership evidence, and procedural approval or notification records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certificate or supporting statement provided to the recipient showing gross payment and tax withheld.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Issue and retain evidence sufficient for the recipient's foreign tax-credit claim and for an Egyptian tax audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold, remit, report, or provide supporting certificates may create primary liability for the Egyptian payer, interest or additional tax, penalties, reassessment of the gross payment, and possible criminal liability where the failure is deliberate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Generally 10% on dividends distributed by an Egyptian company, subject to a possible 5% rate for qualifying listed-share investments and statutory conditions. Treaty rates may be lower and depend on the relevant Egypt double-tax agreement, ownership threshold, holding period, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, identify the treaty article, obtain a valid tax-residence certificate from the recipient's competent foreign authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, document ownership and holding conditions, and submit or retain the information required by the Egyptian Tax Authority and payer procedures. Apply the reduced rate only where Egyptian procedural requirements are satisfied. If the full domestic rate is withheld, the recipient may need to pursue a refund or relief claim through the applicable ETA process. Treaty relief is not available for conduit entities, artificial arrangements, or payments failing the principal-purpose or anti-abuse test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Egyptian withholding rate for many payments of interest, royalties, and similar amounts to non-residents is generally 20%, subject to statutory classification and applicable treaty relief. Egypt treaties commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding rates, but the actual rate is treaty-specific and may be subject to beneficial ownership, maximum-rate, permanent-establishment, government-recipient, and anti-abuse conditions. Payments for software, cloud access, advertising, platform services, technical support, data, and digital services must be classified separately; a payment described as a royalty is not automatically treated as a service, and a service is not automatically exempt from withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Egyptian transfer-pricing documentation commonly requires a Local File where aggregate related-party transactions exceed EGP 8 million during the relevant financial year, subject to the applicable transaction categories and current ETA rules. A Master File is generally relevant to Egyptian members of multinational enterprise groups meeting the applicable consolidated-revenue threshold, commonly EGP 3 billion or more. Country-by-Country reporting obligations may also apply at the multinational-group level, generally using the EGP 3 billion consolidated-revenue threshold and applicable filing or notification rules. Thresholds and administrative requirements must be reconfirmed for the filing year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not generally operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime applicable to every holding, finance, or IP entity. Nevertheless, substance is relevant under transfer-pricing rules, general anti-avoidance principles, beneficial-ownership analysis, treaty anti-abuse provisions, permanent-establishment rules, deductibility rules, and Egyptian commercial and tax administration. The LLC should maintain Egyptian decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or documented operating arrangements, local books, bank and payment controls, inventory and fulfillment evidence, customer and supplier contracts, and commercially credible functions and risks. A nominal Egyptian entity receiving foreign group charges without personnel, control, benefit, or documentary support is high risk.
controlled_transaction_controls: Prepare an intercompany transaction register covering goods, services, royalties, loans, guarantees, reimbursements, cost-sharing, and platform arrangements.
Apply a transaction-specific functional, asset, and risk analysis rather than relying on a group-wide markup.
Benchmark Egyptian distribution or marketing returns using current financial data and document tested-party selection.
Use written agreements that match actual conduct, invoicing, cash settlement, and contractual risk allocation.
Reconcile Local File, Master File, CbCR notification, financial statements, income tax return, VAT records, and withholding declarations.
Retain records in Arabic or with reliable Arabic translations where required by the ETA and preserve them for the statutory audit and assessment period.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Shopify, PayPal, Stripe, bank, cash-on-delivery, marketplace, or foreign settlement revenue; issuing false invoices; maintaining double books; inflating expenses; or deliberately understating taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid tax, additional tax, civil penalties, and criminal tax-evasion sanctions under the Egyptian Income Tax Law, potentially including imprisonment and a fine linked to the tax evaded. The precise sanction depends on the offense, amount, intent, repetition, and applicable amendments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers, authorized signatories, accountants, or beneficial owners who participate in intentional evasion may face personal criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, civil restitution, asset measures, and possible travel restrictions by competent judicial or prosecutorial order. Corporate limited liability is not a defense to personal criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold or remit tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying foreign affiliates, licensors, lenders, consultants, or service providers without applying required Egyptian withholding tax or without filing and remitting the withheld amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian LLC may become liable for the unwithheld tax, additional tax, penalties, reassessment, and related procedural sanctions. Deliberate retention or misappropriation of withheld tax can create criminal exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and signatories may be personally exposed where they authorized, directed, or knowingly permitted the failure. Travel restrictions and imprisonment require competent legal process and are not automatic consequences of an ordinary computational error.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register when required, omission of taxable sales, fabricated purchase invoices, unsupported input-VAT recovery, improper zero-rating, or failure to reconcile platform and payment-processor records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, denial of input credit, additional tax, administrative fines, closure or other administrative measures where legally available, and criminal sanctions for deliberate fraud or evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and authorized representatives may face personal liability for knowing participation in fraudulent invoicing or deliberate VAT evasion, including fines, restitution, and imprisonment under the applicable criminal provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length import prices, management fees, royalties, financing charges, or loss allocations to shift Egyptian profit offshore; failing to prepare required documentation; or filing inconsistent transaction values.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA adjustment to arm's-length income, denial or limitation of deductions, additional corporate tax, withholding-tax exposure, penalties, interest, and documentation-related consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability generally arises from fraud, deliberate falsification, or knowing authorization rather than from a good-faith pricing disagreement. Evidence of engineered losses or fabricated comparables materially increases criminal and civil risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, nominee ownership, or beneficial-ownership concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominee shareholders, undisclosed beneficial owners, circular entities, sham invoices, or an entity with no credible commercial activity to conceal control, source of funds, or profit ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, anti-money-laundering investigation, confiscation or asset-freezing measures where authorized, corporate and licensing consequences, and criminal sanctions for fraud, forgery, tax evasion, or money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, nominees, ultimate beneficial owners, and professional facilitators may face personal criminal liability, fines, imprisonment, restitution, asset restraint, and judicially ordered travel bans. Limited liability does not protect a person who uses the company as an instrument of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and proceeds of crime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving unexplained third-party payments, layering proceeds through payment processors or related entities, falsifying trade documents, disguising illicit funds as inventory or marketing expenses, or ignoring suspicious customer and supplier activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Egyptian anti-money-laundering legislation may impose imprisonment, substantial fines, confiscation, asset freezing, and other measures, with enhanced consequences for organized or predicate-offense conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance personnel may be personally liable for knowing participation, assistance, concealment, or intentional failure to report suspicious activity where a reporting obligation applies. Travel restrictions and pretrial or precautionary measures may be imposed through competent authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using personal accounts, undeclared offshore merchant accounts, false payment descriptions, unauthorized collection structures, or informal remittance channels to avoid banking, tax, customs, or AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential banking, foreign-exchange, customs, tax, AML, and payment-services sanctions, including fines, transaction restrictions, seizure, account action, and criminal prosecution depending on the conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and controllers may face personal investigation, fines, imprisonment, restitution, asset restrictions, and travel limitations where they authorized or knowingly benefited from unlawful payment arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-invoicing imported inventory, misclassifying goods, concealing royalties or assists, splitting shipments to avoid controls, or importing through an entity different from the commercial importer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs reassessment, duties, VAT, fines, seizure, forfeiture, delayed release, and criminal customs liability in cases of deliberate smuggling or fraudulent declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, customs representatives, and beneficial owners may be personally liable for knowing false declarations, smuggling, or document forgery, including criminal sanctions and asset or travel measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining inaccurate ledgers, destroying invoices or settlement records, backdating intercompany agreements, fabricating board approvals, or failing to preserve statutory books and tax evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax assessments, rejection of deductions, administrative penalties, audit escalation, and criminal sanctions for forgery, fraud, or intentional obstruction of tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, accountants, and authorized representatives who approve or use falsified records may face personal criminal and civil liability, including restitution, fines, imprisonment, and judicial precautionary measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, royalties, or service payments through a treaty-country entity lacking commercial substance or beneficial ownership solely to obtain reduced Egyptian withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, application of domestic withholding tax, additional tax, penalties, interest, and potential anti-avoidance or fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal exposure arises where directors knowingly implement sham arrangements, false residence representations, or fraudulent documentation. Good-faith reliance on properly verified treaty documentation is materially different from deliberate treaty shopping.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting Egyptian sales, warehousing, fulfillment, customer support, or contract conclusion through personnel or agents while asserting that only a foreign company operates in Egypt and the Egyptian LLC has no relevant activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential registration, corporate income tax, VAT, payroll, withholding, customs, and interest assessments, together with penalties for non-registration or non-filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability is principally triggered by deliberate concealment, false filings, or obstruction. Directors may face fines and criminal proceedings where the facts meet statutory offense elements.
